notes: NEW ROW, and it is the FOURTH distinct selection encoding found in this app: fill-tint on chip grids (TF-0074, TYPE-0083), checkmark in list popovers (REPLAY-0006), inverted row here and in the sort menu, and a filled/active toolbar button in the replay toolbar. TradingView is internally inconsistent about how it says 'this one is selected'. For the accessibility argument this cuts BOTH ways - the inverted row is the strongest of the four (contrast plus position), and the fill-only chips are the weakest.

notes: NOT EXERCISED - no layout was deleted. NEW ROW, and a debatable choice worth flagging in BOTH directions. In its favour: no hidden swipe gesture to discover, and TradingView elsewhere guards destructive actions with a native alert (REPLAY-0011), so a confirmation is very likely. Against: a 44px destructive target sits permanently beside a 44px open target on every row of a scrolling list, on a phone, including on the layout you are currently working in. This is the kind of density-versus-safety trade UCT will have to make if it ships a mobile layout manager.

notes: STAR STAR THIS IS THE MECHANISM BEHIND LAYOUT-0023, CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY ON A SECOND CLIENT. The mobile Save tile is not a bespoke mobile behaviour - it is the SAME Autosave setting, and the phone honours it. The desktop menu also proved the sync direction end to end: the RECENTLY USED entry for this layout read 'AAPL, 1D' on desktop, matching what the PHONE had saved minutes earlier, while the stale desktop tab was still rendering SPY. So a mobile edit reaches the desktop's server state within seconds. THAT is what 'the workspace travels with the user' means concretely: auto-commit on the phone, account-level storage, and every client reading the same record.

notes: STAR TWO FINDINGS. (a) The list is labelled RECENT SYMBOLS but contains seven major world indices, while this account's ACTUAL symbol-search recents were XAUUSD and MNQ futures contracts (SYMBOL-0050). So Compare seeds a BENCHMARK set - the things you would actually compare against - and the label is doing the honest thing badly. Empty-state design lesson: never show an empty compare box; show the benchmarks. (b) The placeholder accepts ISIN and CUSIP here, whereas the main symbol search advertises equation entry instead - so TradingView TUNES THE PLACEHOLDER TO THE TASK rather than reusing one search component's copy everywhere. UCT has no compare/overlay on mobile at all: MISSING, root cause MISSING_CAPABILITY, though lightweight-charts supports additional series cheaply so a percentage-overlay compare is a realistic v1.
